title: Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy Conditions on the Schedule of Underlying Insurance
content:
**Condition A: underlying limits.** Every exposure the Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy extends over must be scheduled as underlying with at least the tier's required limit for its line: the required homeowners limit, the required condominium limit, the required renters limit, the required landlord dwelling limit, the required auto bodily injury per person limit together with the required auto bodily injury per accident limit and the required auto property damage limit, or the required watercraft limit.

**Condition B: declarations details.** An underlying policy is scheduled only with its policy number, carrier and limits exactly as on its declarations page.

## Condition A restated line by line

| Line of the underlying policy | Limit that must meet the tier minimum |
|---|---|
| Homeowners | Coverage E |
| Condominium | Personal liability |
| Renters | Personal liability |
| Landlord dwelling | Premises liability |
| Auto | Bodily injury per person, bodily injury per accident and property damage, all three |
| Watercraft | Liability |

Each minimum is the figure for the line in the column of the umbrella's own tier. An auto policy meets Condition A only when all three of its limits meet their minimums; meeting one or two is not enough.

## Condition B explained

- The details scheduled are those shown on the underlying policy's declarations page: its policy number, its carrier and its limits.
- These details are facts the customer gives from the declarations page. They are entered exactly as they appear there, without rounding a limit or abbreviating a policy number.
- Condition B applies whatever the carrier of the underlying policy: a Larkspur policy and another carrier's policy are scheduled the same way.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- *Hypothetical:* on a tier whose auto minimums are 250,000 per person, 500,000 per accident and 100,000 property damage, an auto policy with 250,000, 500,000 and 100,000 meets Condition A; an auto policy with 250,000, 300,000 and 100,000 does not, because its per accident limit is below the minimum.
- *Hypothetical:* a declarations page showing a liability limit of 300,000 is scheduled with a limit of 300,000, and the policy number is scheduled character for character as printed.
